objective.label: Capture the Bagration flèches and the Great Redoubt.

battlefield.note: The Kolocha along the north, the Great Redoubt on the Kurgan height, Bagration's flèches on a low rise, the Semyonovka ravine and the Utitsa woods to the south.

popup.title: Borodino: The Great Redoubt
popup.body:
You command Napoleon's Grand Army in front of the Russian earthworks on the road to Moscow. Send Davout and Ney at Bagration's flèches and Eugène across from Borodino at the Great Redoubt, with the voltigeurs ahead and the cuirassiers ready to ride into any gap. The forts and the ravine favour the defender: attack together, not one corps at a time.

Objective: Capture the Bagration flèches and the Great Redoubt.

At Borodino on 7 September 1812 Napoleon's army stormed the Russian earthworks after a day of repeated assaults: Bagration's flèches fell in the morning and the Great Redoubt in the afternoon, at terrible cost on both sides. Kutuzov withdrew in good order, and a week later the French entered Moscow.

popup.title: The grand battery
popup.body: A hundred French guns open fire on the flèches at dawn. Send Davout and Ney at the flèches, and Eugène at the Great Redoubt.

popup.title: Bagration counterattacks
popup.body: Russian grenadiers and cuirassiers are coming forward from Semyonovskaya to retake the flèches.

popup.title: The Cossack raid
popup.body: Platov's Cossacks and Uvarov's cavalry have crossed the Kolocha upstream and are riding on Borodino behind your left. Turn something to meet them.

popup.title: Caulaincourt's cuirassiers
popup.body: General Caulaincourt's cuirassiers are ready to ride into the back of the Great Redoubt while the infantry storms it from the front.

popup.title: The Russian reserves
popup.body: Kutuzov sends his last reserves from Gorki to retake the Great Redoubt.
